title: CHAPTER THIRTY-NINE. On the permission of sin, its foundation, opposite, connections, and consequences
latin: CAPUT TRIGESIMUM NONUM, De permissione peccati, eiusque fundamento, opposito, connexis et consequentibus. HActenus de peccato: sequitur eius PERMISSIO, quae est actus divinae providentiae circa illud, quo omnia impedimenta quae Deus novit, si adhiberentur potentiae aut voluntati hominis, peccatum reipsa impeditura, tum cogentia quae efficaciter impellunt ad agendum a quo quis abhorret, suspenduntur. Locum hunc de permissione inquisivit doctissimus Twissus; Arminius quoque non semel tentavit. Ignoratio huius doctrinae efficit ut cum quidam intelligere non possent unde peccatum sit, utpote summum malum quod datur, quod a Deo summe bono esse nequit, ipsam Dei providentiam negaverint.
english: CHAPTER THIRTY-NINE. On the permission of sin, and its foundation, opposite, connections, and consequences.

Thus far concerning sin: next follows its PERMISSION, which is an act of divine providence concerning it, by which all impediments that God knows would, if applied to the humans power or will, really impede the sin, and also compelling forces that efficaciously drive toward doing what one abhors, are suspended. This locus on permission the most learned Twisse inquired into; Arminius also attempted it more than once. Ignorance of this doctrine makes it that when some could not understand whence sin is — inasmuch as it is the highest evil that is given, which cannot be from God who is most highly good — they denied Gods providence itself.

title: VI–III. What to weigh in permission; foundation in free choice and Gods wisdom and power
latin: VI. Est autem in permissione peccati expendendum illius fundamentum, oppositum, connexa, et circa peccati progressum et consummationem consequentia. III. Fundamentum est partim libertas arbitrii, quam creaturae rationali Deus creator indidit, et cuius usum constantia datoris creaturae isti adimi haud patitur; partim infinita Dei sapientia et potentia, qua scit et potest e malo bonum producere. Hinc Deus permittit quicquid permittit: non inscienter virium et affectus creaturarum, quia omnia novit; non invitus, potuisset enim creaturam non producere quae esset liberi arbitrii, et posset productam in nihilum redigere aut varie mutare.
english: VI. In the permission of sin there is to be weighed its foundation, opposite, connections, and the consequences around the progress and consummation of sin. III. The foundation is partly the liberty of choice that God the creator planted in the rational creature, and whose use the Givers constancy does not allow to be taken from that creature; partly Gods infinite wisdom and power, by which He knows and can produce good from evil.

Hence God permits whatever He permits: not unknowingly of creatures powers and affection, because He knows all things; not unwillingly, for He could have not produced a creature that would be of free choice, and could reduce one produced to nothing or variously change it.

title: IV–VIII. Opposite of permission: impediment and coercion; kinds of impediment
latin: IV. Oppositum permissionis est impeditio et coactio. Impeditio est, qua potentiae et voluntati creaturae impedimentum ponitur ne peccet. Coactio est, qua quis efficaciter impellitur ad agendum a quo abhorret. VI. Efficientiae ratione est aut efficax aut inefficax. VII. Obiecti ratione ponitur impedimentum vel potentiae vel voluntati. VIII. Impedimentum potestati positum tollit facultatem; voluntati positum, absque tollenda facultate, flectit aut retinet. Permissio non est lex positiva peccati, nec Deus author peccati; sed suspensio impedimentorum et non-impeditio actus creaturae liberè peccantis.
english: IV. The opposite of permission is impediment and coercion. Impediment is that by which an obstacle is set to the creatures power and will lest it sin. Coercion is that by which someone is efficaciously driven toward doing what he abhors. VI. By reason of efficiency it is either efficacious or inefficacious. VII. By reason of the object an impediment is set either to power or to will. VIII. An impediment set to power takes away the faculty; one set to will, without taking away the faculty, bends or holds it back. Permission is not a positive law of sin, nor is God the author of sin; but the suspension of impediments and the non-impeding of the act of a creature freely sinning.

title: XII–XVI. Connections of permission; direction of sin by providence
latin: XII. Connexa permissioni in principio, progressu, et fine sunt: praescientia, decretum, ordinatio, directio, et determinatio. XVI. Directio est divina providentia qua actus peccati, licet a creatura malus, a Deo ordinatur ad fines bonos, sive in obiectum sive in finem. Exempla: Ioseph a fratribus venditus (Gen. 45:8); Iob a Satana afflictus (Iob 1-2); David et Absalom (2 Sam. 12; 15-16). Deus dicitur facere mala quae ab hominibus sceleratis et ab ipso Satana patrantur, quia partes potissimae in actionibus istis dirigendo et determinando Dei fuerunt, et quia nocendi potentia non amplius effecit quam Deus determinavit.
english: XII. Connected to permission in beginning, progress, and end are: foreknowledge, decree, ordination, direction, and determination. XVI. Direction is the divine providence by which the act of sin, though evil from the creature, is ordered by God toward good ends — whether toward an object or toward an end. Examples: Joseph sold by his brothers (Genesis 45:8); Job afflicted by Satan (Job 1-2); David and Absalom (2 Samuel 12; 15-16). God is said to do evils wrought by wicked humans and by Satan himself, because the chief parts in those actions by directing and determining were Gods, and because the power of harming effected no more than God determined.

title: XVIII–XX. Direction into object and end; determination of sin; Cap. 39 close
latin: XVIII. Directio in obiectum est, quando Deus peccatoris actionem ita moderatur ut in hoc, non in illud, obiectum cadat — ut Davidi permisit statuere de Nabale, sed non permisit fundere sanguinem innocentem (1 Sam. 25); permisit confugere ad Achis et stultitiam simulare, sed non pugnare contra Israel (1 Sam. 21; 27; 29). XIX. Directio in finem est, quando Deus ex peccato elicit finem bonum, sive iustitiae sive misericordiae. XX. Determinatio peccati est actus providentiae quo Deus circumscribit mensuram, tempus, modum, et terminum peccati, ne ultra quam ipse vult grassari possit (1 Cor. 10:13; 2 Cor. 4:8-9). Ita Deus permittendo non desinit regnare, nec peccatum evadit extra providentiae limites.
english: XVIII. Direction into an object is when God so moderates the sinners action that it falls on this object, not that — as He permitted David to resolve concerning Nabal, but did not permit him to pour out innocent blood (1 Samuel 25); He permitted him to flee to Achish and feign folly, but not to fight against Israel (1 Samuel 21; 27; 29). XIX. Direction into an end is when God draws from sin a good end, whether of justice or of mercy.

XX. Determination of sin is the act of providence by which God circumscribes the measure, time, mode, and limit of sin, lest it be able to rage beyond what He Himself wills (1 Corinthians 10:13; 2 Corinthians 4:8-9). Thus God by permitting does not cease to reign, nor does sin escape outside the limits of providence.
